value.rationale: Rooted cluster-size distributions are a fundamental site-percolation and network-reliability observable. The result is a uniform first-order stochastic comparison of a distinguished nonisomorphic cospectral strongly regular pair for every occupancy probability and every fixed population, with exact strictness boundaries and a closed susceptibility difference. This is not a routine normalization or an isolated scalar computation: it shows which random connectivity information remains unseen by identical spectra and provides a substantive exact finite-media benchmark.
